That is R8's iter-07 shape - a non-discriminating value on every row at a discriminating column's weight.

questions.element: three-colour glyph system as the site's only colour system
questions.evidence: none - concept round, no build (discipline rule 10)
questions.note: Relocation is judged on the surface as it reads, so the verdict waits for pixels. The text-level signal is already strong: the packet withdraws colour from everything else and reinstates it, at higher frequency, on a per-item stamp - noise moved between channels rather than removed, and known_risks[3] concedes a dark-theme contrast problem with --muted.

Judged only from the packet text plus RULES.md R7-R13 and JUDGE.md; no pixel property was scored, nothing below a fold inferred. The R13 challenge was judged as an argument per rule 11; the R8 conflict in q4 and q5 is raised nowhere in the packet, so it is a quiet violation.

findings.problem: A provenance glyph is stamped on every fact, row, claim and paragraph of every template, so on any given surface the mark is near-uniform and carries the page's only colour.
findings.invariant: A provenance glyph renders at a weight above --muted only where its state differs from the collection's default state on that surface.
findings.prescription: Print the surface's default provenance once in its header and stamp only the exceptions, which is the badge clause's own construction.

findings.problem: The gutter occupies the leftmost position on every template, so the first thing the eye meets on an index row is metadata rather than the row's discriminating value.
findings.invariant: On every index surface the row's discriminating value is the leftmost non-decorative element in the reading order.
findings.prescription: Move the stamp to the row's trailing side, where R7 already places metadata, keeping the gutter for prose templates only.

findings.problem: R-D is declined outright: the packet states that catalog@390 is untouched and that the requirement stands on the other three concepts, so this concept offers no answer to the brief's one measured findability target.
findings.invariant: Each concept answers R-D or argues why its bet excludes it; deferring to sibling packets is not an answer a keeper can rule on.
findings.prescription: State the minimum catalog treatment the gutter implies at 390, even if it is only that the gutter is suppressed there.

findings.problem: The gutter takes over the home rail's date track, so the changed feed's temporal signal and the provenance stamp compete for one column with no stated precedence.
findings.invariant: The home feed's per-item date remains readable as a date at 1440 and 390 with the gutter present.
findings.prescription: Keep the feed date in the rail and put the glyph inline with the item, rather than merging two meanings into one track.

diagnosis.strongest: HIER on the prose templates - the reading column stays prose-first, F-K12 is explicit, and moving the fact stamp into the gutter is the round's cleanest stated resolution of S18's dead second column.
diagnosis.weakest: DENS - the concept's whole identity is a mark repeated on every item of every surface, declared as one global policy with no R8 class assigned anywhere.
diagnosis.critical_issue: The glyph is a non-discriminating value rendered at the site's only coloured weight on every row, which is the exact shape R8's iter-07 addendum forbids, and the packet raises no K14 challenge against R8 - so it is a quiet violation, not an argument.
diagnosis.highest_value_improvement: Print each surface's default provenance once in its header and stamp only the exceptions; that keeps the honesty claim, removes the uniform chrome, and restores the discriminating value to the first landing on every index.

downstream.weakness: The strongest idea in the round about trust is attached to the weakest decision in the round about chrome.
downstream.cause: Provenance is treated as a property of every item rather than as an exception worth marking, so its frequency is set by the corpus rather than by what a reader needs.
downstream.recommendation: The default-plus-exception form is a small change that preserves the bet; a finalist built on the per-item form should not be built before it is made.
